text:
alex: CI perf test failed on PR #5023 — microbench diff exceeded threshold, marking as flaky/regression. cc @jia @maria
ci-bot: perf-check: PR 5023: microbench/kv_cache_hit_rate: -12.4% (threshold -5%) ; microbench/batch_latency_p95: +18ms (threshold +10ms) — status: FAIL
jia: ack. which commit in the PR touched kernel selection or batching heuristics?
alex: PR touches: kernel_selector.rs and batch_scheduler.py. commits: 1) 2f9c4d6 kernel heuristics tweak, 2) 7a1b2c3 doc only. Bisect points to 2f9c4d6 locally.
maria: can you paste the CI perf output snippet?
alex: sure:
```
---- perf summary ----
microbench/kv_cache_hit_rate: baseline 0.893 -> current 0.783 (-12.4%)
microbench/batch_latency_p95: baseline 42ms -> current 60ms (+42.9%)
kernel-selection: chosen kernel="matmul_fused_avx" -> fallback="matmul_generic"
cpu-util: baseline 72% -> current 88%
----------------------
```
sam: whoa fallback kernel on CI — that suggests kernel selector picked wrong path under the new heuristic. maybe sequence-length distribution changed?
jia: I repro'd end-to-end with a CI-sized trace: selector score function prefers single-threaded path when cpu-util > 80% in the heuristic we added. The heuristic threshold is 0.8 (80%). With CI containers noisy, it flips.
maria: that explains the latency bump and lower KV hit rate (evictions due to slower processing). can we tighten selector to prefer vectorized kernels unless memory pressure high?
alex: quick fix candidate: revert the heuristic commit 2f9c4d6 or make it env-gated for CI (disable by REDWOOD_PERF_SAFE_MODE). Which approach is safer for rollout?
sre-bot: rollout blocked: perf-regression > threshold detected — cannot promote PR to staging until resolved.
sam: revert is fastest to unblock. We can open a follow-up to rework heuristics with better noise handling.
jia: doing local revert now and will push a hotfix branch. tagging @maria for review of follow-up.
alex: thanks. after revert, let's add a microbenchmark that exercises kernel selector under noisy CPU to avoid future flakes. also add an integration perf test that asserts kernel choice distribution stays within expected percentile.
maria: agree. also add CI guard: if perf delta occurs but is due to kernel fallback, mark for manual review instead of auto-fail for a day while we triage? maybe dangerous but reduces churn.
sam: prefer automated guard: if fallback kernel logged, fail with 'flaky-kernel' label and auto-annotate PR with suggested action (revert or tune).
jia: pushed revert branch: PR 5026. CI running.
ci-bot: PR 5026: perf-check: running...
alex: nice. once 5026 green we'll fast-revert 5023 and re-evaluate heuristic redesign.
maria: filed issue #1249 to redesign kernel selector scoring: include KV cache impact and avoid hard CPU-util threshold.
sre-bot: note: this thread marked as rollout-blocker until revert merges or perf regression fixed. :warning:
alex: thanks everyone — follow-up action items in #eng-runtime backlog. :thumbsup:
